subject: Orchid Labs — post-demo latency/throughput notes and next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Reyes <amelia@orchidlabs.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Orchid demo recap + quick answers

Hi Amelia — great to meet you and the Eng team today. Thanks for the time and for walking through your 3 use cases (search ranking, chat summarization, and realtime recommendations). Per our call, here are the short answers and next steps so things are actionable: 

- Latency profile we saw on the demo model (gpt-redwood-small-quant): median token latency ~9 ms, p95 token latency ~26 ms for 512-token contexts on T4-like VMs.
- Throughput: single GPU sustained ~180 tokens/sec for batch size 8; with our dedicated pooling config you'd see ~3–4x aggregate throughput across 4 GPUs for batched inference.
- Tail behavior: for prompt patterns with long prefix KV cache reuse we saw p99 spikes primarily when cache miss + long generation (>1k tokens); average p99 ~120 ms.

Attachments: I uploaded the quick bench CSV (orchid_bench_q2.csv) and a short PDF summary (orchid_latency_summary.pdf) with per-sequence breakdowns.

Proposed next steps:
1) If the numbers look in line, we can spin up a 14-day dedicated trial with your tokens routed to a tuned pool — Marissa can set this up.
2) Your team had a question about provisioning for bursty arrivals; if you can share expected 95th-percentile request rate per minute, we’ll auto-simulate and propose a config.
3) I’ll follow up with the benchmarking artifacts and a short note on how caching/batching can reduce cost by ~30% on similar workloads.

Ping me if you want anything else clarified — I’ll send the bench artifacts now.

Best,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
(415) 555-0162

--
Attachments: orchid_bench_q2.csv (text/csv), orchid_latency_summary.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Amelia Reyes <amelia@orchidlabs.ai>

Thanks Sean — good recap. A couple quick follow-ups from Eng: 

1) For the p95/p99 numbers you shared, can you provide the exact test harness (sequence lengths, prompt prefixes, beam/temperature settings) so we can run the same locally?
2) What's the 95th percentile end-to-end latency for generation requests where the output is ~400 tokens (not per-token)? We care about tail latency for user-facing responses.

If you can send a small reproducible bench or the script, that would help us evaluate during the week.

Appreciate it,
Amelia

amelia@orchidlabs.ai

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Reyes <amelia@orchidlabs.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orchid demo recap + quick answers

Hi Amelia — thanks for the clear items. Attached are the test harness notes and the raw results we ran for the demo: orchid_bench_q2.csv and orchid_latency_summary.pdf. Quick highlights below so you don't need to dig immediately: 

- Test harness: single-request generation using prompt templates with 128-token prefix and target outputs of 100/200/400 tokens. Model: gpt-redwood-small-quant. Decode settings: temperature=0.0, top_p=0.95, no beam search, greedy sampling for deterministic bench.
- E2E (client-request to last-token) median / p95 / p99 for ~400-token outputs (measured on a T4-like single card): 310ms / 720ms / 1,150ms.
- For multi-GPU dedicated pool with batching (batch size 8, 4 GPUs), simulated E2E p95 ~220ms and p99 ~380ms (these are our internal simulated tail reductions due to batching + prefix cache reuse).
- Notes: p99 spikes were correlated with cache cold-starts for very long prompts and with concurrent background maintenance tasks in the VM image — we observed improvement after a tuned kernel selection and warm-up.

If useful, we can provide the exact jupyter bench notebook and the dockerfile to reproduce locally. Marissa (cc) can set up temporary trial access if you'd like to run this end-to-end against your payloads.

Let me know if you'd like a quick 20-min pairing session to run the bench together.

Best,
Sean

--
Attachments: orchid_bench_q2.csv (text/csv), orchid_latency_summary.pdf (application/pdf)

Hi Amelia — quick bump in case this got buried. I sent the harness and numbers on Friday but haven’t heard back from your Eng team. Two quick asks so we can keep momentum: 

1) Are those p95/p99 numbers in the right ballpark for your SLA planning? If not, which target should we optimize for (e.g., p95 < 300ms for 400-token outputs)?
2) Are you still targeting a July pilot start? If yes, Marissa can provision a 14-day dedicated trial and we’ll seed it with the tuned pool config used in the sims.

If it's easier, we can also schedule a 20-min working session next week to walk through the jupyter bench and reproduce the numbers together. If your priorities shifted, a one-line update is totally fine.

Thanks — hoping to sync before budgets lock.

Cheers,
Sean
